craft_claim: Distrust asserted without a recoverable stated claim to deflate — or nihilism staged as decoration — reads as posturing: the stance must answer something, and hostile irony carries documented relational costs, so unconditional cynicism fails as craft and as ethics.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 110(1):116-132
supporting_evidence.note: Cynicism is a costly disposition with correlates, not a free pose; a text that models chronic distrust without warrant imports that cost while delivering no recognition payoff.

The Humor Styles Questionnaire classifies aggressive humor — sarcasm and ridicule — among potentially maladaptive styles associated with poorer relational outcomes, a documented cost of hostile irony aimed at persons.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 70(6):1164-1184
supporting_evidence.note: Because suspicion itself reallocates attribution toward ulterior causes, an unearned suspicious voice dramatizes systematic misreading: the posture generates the corruption it claims only to observe.

counterevidence.note: The same instrument distinguishes adaptive styles (affiliative, self-enhancing) from aggressive ones and reports personality-level associations; the documented cost attaches to hostile usage and repeated style, not to a single ironic line.

scope: Any sustained cynical register; the tone's primary failure diagnostic (card section 7).
exceptions: When the pose itself is the subject — a narrator whose cynicism the text goads — posturing becomes content and the failure inverts into technique.
Misanthropic accumulation is convention, not failure, in forms built for it (Menippean overload; the satirical mode's invective tradition).
